content_preview.title: MLX 0.32.4 Adds Attention and Gated Delta Net Gradients, Metal 1-Bit Affine Quantization and Python 3.15 Wheels
content_preview.summary: Apple's MLX array framework shipped v0.32.4 on October 14 with training-oriented VJPs, 1-bit affine quantization on CPU and Metal, Python 3.15 support and stft/istft.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The MLX array framework published v0.32.4 on October 14, 2026, according to the [GitHub release page](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx/releases/tag/v0.32.4). The release notes list 97 change entries and a "New Contributors" section naming 24 first-time contributors, by a count of the lines in the notes. Headline entries include gradient (VJP) support for scaled dot product attention and for the gated delta net, 1-bit affine quantization on Metal, Python 3.15 support and new short-t...

editor_notes.content_quality: Clear Briefing (561 words, range 300-800). Lead covers release date and counts, then one section per headline feature, then a short list of other entries and a 'What We Don't Know' section. Appropriate technical depth for a developer audience; benchmark figures are labelled as the PR authors' self-reported results.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 6 sources are first-party GitHub (ml-explore/mlx), a legitimate primary source type for a release briefing; none is independent of the subject, which is acceptable for a Briefing. Snapshots read from sources/2026-10/mlx-0324-.../ (source-0..5.html.gz, all HTTP 200, 300-820 KB, not thin, no archive fallback, no suspicious_patterns in the manifest). I additionally re-fetched the live data via the GitHub API as a cross-check. source-0 (release v0.32.4): published_at 2026-10-14T23:37:14Z (created 20:07Z), not draft or prerelease; recounted from the raw release body: 97 bullet lines under 'What's Changed' and 24 under 'New Contributors' (snapshot also shows 24 'made their first contribution' lines). Both counts match the article, and the article correctly attributes them to a count of the notes' lines rather than to GitHub or Apple. The notes list all five feature PRs: #4563 (Adding VJP for the scaled dot product attention, by @tpegolotti), #4565 (Adding VJP for gated delta net, @tpegolotti), #3161 (Add 1-bit affine quantization support (Metal), @khosravipasha, listed as a first-time contributor), #4555 (Add Python 3.15 and 3.15t support, @XXXXRT666), #3639 (Add stft and istft to mlx.core.fft, @eyupcanakman). GitHub API shows all five PRs merged to main (4563 on 2026-09-29, 4565 on 09-29, 4555 on 09-29, 3161 on 2026-10-09, 3639 on 2026-10-10) before the v0.32.4 release on 10-14, so the older low-numbered PRs 3161 and 3639 were genuinely included in 0.32.4, not merely referenced. source-1 (#4563): quotes 'needed for fine-tuning and training', 'uses a lot of memory since it allocates a full [context_size x context_size] attention matrix', 'For the causal case we have up to 2.8x speedups', 'up to 24x at the longest shape: 24.63 GiB to 1 GiB for batch size = 1' are verbatim (the 24.63 GiB to 1 GiB figure is for batch 1; batch 4 is 97GiB to 4GiB); M5 Ultra, 80 cores confirmed; the exception '(256, 24, 4) ... can be slower than the fallback' with better memory, and the trailing Edit about later commits improving memory and speedup, are accurately reported; 'tiled matmuls' confirmed. All figures are the author's own, as the article says. source-2 (#4565): quote 'one for the sequential case (pure metal kernel) and one for the chunked case (using neural accelerator)' verbatim; '1.4x to 6.3x faster than the sequential one and 9x to 79x faster than the fallback', batch sizes 1, 4, 8 and sequence lengths 8 to 4096 confirmed. source-3 (#3161): bit-widths {2,3,4,5,6,8} to {1,2,3,4,5,6,8}, CPU and Metal backends including quantize/dequantize/qmm, 'assumes the model has already been quantized externally (e.g. during training)' and 'not yet supported on the CUDA backend' confirmed (the article's quote drops only the bold markup). The PR also contains hypothetical tok/s tables and kernel benchmarks, which the article correctly does not repeat. source-4 (#4555): Python 3.15 and 3.15t added to the release wheel matrix, nanobind 3.0.1 to 3.1.0 confirmed. Note the PR carries an AI usage disclosure ('All tests are generated by AI'); not relevant to the article's claims. source-5 (#3639): signature follows torch.stft except norm takes the 'backward'/'ortho'/'forward' strings, confirmed. Other-entries paragraph (FloorDivide primitive for integer floor division #4642, minmax #4674, Metal extension build support #4004, fp_gather_qmv for gather_qmm on CUDA #4508, MLX_CONV_WINOGRAD #4639, cooperative tensor build issues on Mac OS 27 #4594) each matches a release-note line; the 'many concern views, strides and contiguity flags' characterisation is fair. Title wording 'Gradients' is supported: both #4563 and #4565 add VJPs (reverse-mode gradients); the 'Metal' qualifier for 1-bit matches PR #3161's title; 'Python 3.15 Wheels' matches #4555 (release wheel matrix). Summary's 'CPU and Metal' for 1-bit is supported by the PR body even though the PR/release title says (Metal). Attribution of each feature to the correct PR number verified. No orphan URLs: every URL in the body is in article.sources and vice versa.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every number, date, quote and attribution checked individually against the snapshots and the live GitHub API; no discrepancies found. Date October 14, 2026 matches the release publish date (UTC).
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. No promotional language; the caveat about the slower (256, 24, 4) configuration and the 'What We Don't Know' section are balanced. No AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: No existing Herald article covers MLX v0.32.4 or any MLX release; the only MLX mentions are in an August Apple Core AI article and an Ollama release article, a different story. New topic.
recommendations: Optionally cite an independent outlet if one covers the release; not required for a first-party-documented Briefing.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-attributed release briefing; counts verified by recount, benchmarks labelled as self-reported, all features tied to the correct merged PRs that are in the release. Ready for publication. Featured candidacy: 1 - accurate release coverage of a minor-version ML framework update for a defined Apple-silicon developer audience
